string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and one of the four direct-administered municipalities. With a history spanning over three thousand years, it has served as the political and cultural center of China for centuries. The city is home to iconic landmarks such as the Great Wall, the Forbidden City, and Tiananmen Square. As a global metropolis, Beijing combines ancient traditions with modern development, hosting numerous international organizations and Fortune 500 companies. The city covers an area of approximately 16,410 square kilometers and has a population of over 21 million people.

Shanghai is one of the four direct-administered municipalities and the largest city in China by population. Located at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it serves as a global financial hub and a major center for international trade. The city is renowned for its stunning skyline, particularly the Bund and Pudong districts with landmarks like the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower. Shanghai has a rich history as a treaty port and has evolved into a modern metropolis while preserving its unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures. It covers approximately 6,340 square kilometers.

Chongqing is the largest of the four direct-administered municipalities and one of the most populous cities in the world. Located in southwestern China at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, it is known as the Mountain City due to its unique hilly terrain. Chongqing has a rich history dating back over three thousand years and served as China\'s wartime capital during World War II. Today, it is a major economic center and transportation hub, famous for its spicy hotpot cuisine, dramatic night views, and rapid urban development. The municipality covers an area of approximately 82,400 square kilometers.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality located in northern China, bordering Beijing and the Bohai Sea. As one of China\'s largest coastal cities, it serves as a major port and industrial center. Tianjin has a distinctive colonial architectural heritage, particularly in its Five Great Avenues district, reflecting its history as a treaty port. The city is known for its traditional culture, including Tianjin opera and cross-talk comedy. With a population of over 13 million, Tianjin plays a crucial role in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei economic region and continues to develop as a hub for advanced manufacturing and innovation.
